_why: Editorial rewrites of fact notes whose bare numbers collide with values of other jurisdictions' facts (C46 unbound) or are pipeline-internal. Meaning preserved; dropped numbers are restatements of the bound value or derivation scaffolding.
md.pit.rates: The two top bands are new from the 2025 Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act and apply to 2026 withholding [US-MDS5-003]. The 2% capital-gain surcharge applies at assessment only.
md.wh.method: The single bases of the 3.30 table reproduce from the state bands plus the county rate; the joint bases reproduce exactly. Per-period exemption / standard deduction: weekly 61.54/65.38, monthly 266.67/283.33; the biweekly (130.76) and semimonthly (141.66) standard deductions are truncated; daily amounts divide the annual amounts by 365.
md.wh.std_deduction: TG 10-217: indexed from 2026 and rounded down to a multiple of 50 [US-MDS5-002]; the Comptroller's published adjustment figure was not read.
md.nonres.special_rate: Residents of non-reciprocal states: state rate plus the special nonresident rate, no county tax; the flat nonresident rate is 7.0% (lowest table rate plus the special rate). Residents of reciprocal DC/PA/VA/WV are exempt with Form MW507 [US-MULTI-008]; the exemption is lost if the employee keeps a Maryland abode for more than six months and is present 183 days or more (not WV). Maryland residents working in Delaware or another non-reciprocal state: Delaware table with county tax and credit.
md.sui.employer.rate.min: Experience rates run from the minimum to the maximum ([[FACT:md.sui.employer.rate.max=7.5]] percent), which is also the standard rate; foreign construction contractors pay the industry average.
me.wh.std_deduction.single: Full amount if annual wages are at or below 102,250; otherwise 12,450 x (177,250 - W) / 75,000; zero from 177,250. This is the withholding figure, not the return-level standard deduction.
me.wh.bracket.single.1.ceiling: Single: 5.80% below 27,400; 1,589 + 6.75% to 64,850; 4,117 + 7.15% above. Use the withholding standard deduction (12,450 single / 27,750 married), not the return-level amounts.
me.pfml.rate.total.15_plus: Authority FAQ plus the statutory ceiling [US-MES5-024]: employers with 15 or more employees remit the total rate, of which the employee bears at most [[FACT:me.pfml.employee.max_rate=0.5]] percent; employers with fewer than 15 remit [[FACT:me.pfml.rate.total.under_15=0.5]] percent, all deductible from the employee. From 2028 the department sets the rate by October 1. Wages capped at the Social Security wage base; the employee share is deducted after tax; an employee share paid by the employer is taxable wages; Form W-2 box 14 label 'MEPFML'; late payment 1% of quarterly payroll; coverage follows unemployment-insurance localization.
mi.wh.supplemental.rate: Bonuses and separate payments are withheld at the flat rate with no exemption adjustment (Treasury Guide 446).
mi.local.cities.count: Detroit plus 23 self-administered cities that file on separate city returns (T4). The uniform ordinance sets the default resident and nonresident rates (section MI.6) unless a city resolves a lower rate (MCL 141.611) [US-MIR3-003]. The rates, forms and due dates of the 23 cities are not yet confirmed.
mi.sui.wage_base: MCL 421.44(4): the base of 9,500 is reduced to 9,000 for non-delinquent employers when the trust fund is at least 2.5 billion on the prior June 30 [US-MIS5-010]; delinquent employers keep 9,500. Not CPI-indexed; the 2027 base depends on the fund at 2026-06-30.
mi.leave.esta.accrual.hours_worked_per_h: Earned Sick Time Act (2018, as amended in 2025): every employer; small employers (10 or fewer) cap 40 hours or front-load 40 (from 2025-10-01); others cap 72 or front-load 72; FLSA-exempt employees assumed to work 40 hours; pay at the greater of the base rate or the minimum wage (excluding overtime, bonus, commission and tips); 1-hour increments; new hires may wait up to 120 days; no payout; rehire within 2 months restores the balance; documentation for absences over 3 days; records kept 3 years.
mo.pit.bracket.8.rate: Applies over 9,436; reconciles to the statutory top rate after the two statutory reductions (US-MOS5-018).
mo.pit.oracle.example_1.annual_tax: Department of Revenue example, married, spouse works, wages 35,000: taxable income 18,900; the Department's rounded tax on the lower brackets plus 9,464 x 4.7% gives 707.81 a year and 59 a month. Unrounded lower brackets give 707.67; the annual residual disappears in period rounding.
mo.sui.wages.401k_included: 401(k) deferrals are unemployment wages; cafeteria-plan salary reductions are not.
nc.labour.minwage.state.follows_federal: Higher of the state statutory floor or the FLSA rate (7.25 in 2026, Annex FED); no state indexation.
nj.sui.wages.401k_included: 401(k) deferrals and cafeteria-plan reductions are included where cash is electable; dependent-care assistance and personal use of a company car are also included.
nm.pit.oracle.example_1.withholding: FYI-104 weekly, married, wages 1,000: the bracket base tax plus 4.3% of the 210 excess gives 21.80; adding the 20.00 extra withholding requested by the employee gives 41.80.
mt.minwage.hourly: Indexed: 10.55 x 1.0292 = 10.86, rounded to the nearest 0.05 = 10.85 (US-MTS5-016).
me.exempt.salary.weekly_min: Annualised pay must exceed 3,000 x the state minimum wage (or the FLSA level): 3,000 x 15.10 / 52 = 871.1538, published as 871.16 (first cent above). Safe rule: the salary must exceed 3,000 x the minimum wage.
